title: GTA 6 leaker's latest video allegedly shows scenes from the final mission, as they indicate the leaks may have come to an end
summary: Cyberleak is back with another GTA 6 leak they say shows snippets from the game's ending.

Image credit: Rockstar Games News by Sherif Saed Senior Contributor Updated on Oct. 14, 2026, 1:42 p.m. 13 comments Follow Grand Theft Auto VI Prioritise us on Google Cyberleek, the leaker who's been releasing footage from Grand Theft Auto 6 for weeks now, is seemingly done posting leaks. Cyberleek released a new - seemingly final - video today which supposedly shows parts of the game's ending. The leaker has indicated they may be done sharing footage as their goal of pumping their crypto coin had failed. Cyberleek recently said they'd release a 200GB build of the game if the coin hits $30m market cap, which it's nowhere near doing . The coin has crashed in recent weeks after a major bump that coincided with the release of leaked footage showing co-protagonist Lucia fully naked , shortly after they released footage of co-protagonist Jason also nude . Eurogamer has seen the latest footage, and it's not as dramatic as Cyberleek initially made it out to be. The footage does not appear to be of the game's ending sequence or final cutscene, though the location of where the action takes place could be a spoiler. The four-minute video ends with a montage of various locations and flyover footage of a city, set to Journey's Don't Stop Believin'. There may be something there, but when viewed without proper context, it's hard to say what's actually being spoiled. Still, the footage is best avoided if you want to jump into the game fresh. "The 30m was not reached, so no build," Cyberleek reportedly said in a message posted on their website. "Uploading 200+ GB anonymously is a serious risk - worth it only if the milestone funded the secret project." At the time of writing, Cyberleek's memecoin's market cap has dropped to $1.2m just three days after reaching its peak of $7.8m. It also seems they've abandoned the initial plan to tie certain gameplay leaks to the coin's market cap. "The leeks stop here. For now," Cyberleek allegedly wrote, though it's worth keeping in mind that the leaker reappeared last week after going to ground following their initial leaks in August, seemingly in response to Rockstar parent company Take-Two initiating a massive investigation and issuing subpoenas to Discord and Microsoft. Given recent history, Cyberleek could simply re-emerge yet again with a new scam and more footage. GTA 6's 19th November official launch is not far off, however, so their window is closing.
